newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds helped by Treasuries but seen trapped.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds helped by Treasuries but seen trapped.

text.p: German debt prices firmed in early trade on the back of stronger U.S. treasuries overnight, but traders said the market was likely to stay in a very narrow range ahead of key U.S. data due later in the session.

"The market is a tad firmer here after the Fed coupon buying pushed the Treasuries up -- that has produced a bit of a squeeze and helped the tone," said Dirk Aufderheide at DMG futures and options in Frankfurt.
The U.S. Federal Rerserve said late on Monday that it was buying all coupons maturing from May 15, 1999 to March 31, 2002, sparking a light rally in the U.S. market.
By 0640 GMT, the June DTB Bund futures contract was 11 basis points higher on the day at 100.53, having trading an early range of 100.52 to 100.60.
Traders said that with U.S. first-quarter employment costs numbers later, the Bund contract was likely to remain fenced in by a tight range for most of the early part of the session.
Economists polled by Reuters are forecasting the employment cost index will show a 0.9 percent gain for the quarter, slightly higher than the 0.8 percent gain in the fourth quarter of 1996.
But some said the risk was for a stronger number, threatening to hit debt prices hard.
"We're expecting a 1.1 percent gain on the quarter," said Aufderheide.
Traders said the German market was more short than long going into the US data, which limits downside damage somewhat.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark January 2006 Bund was trading at 100.81 by 0650 GMT for a yield of 5.878 percent.
The yield spread between T-notes and Bunds was at 116 basis and expected to remain steady until the release of the U.S. numbers.
